context: Class wrap-up on a unit about economic disparity and historical politics
purpose: Teach: 獲得/不幸/素人/格差/日経/人達/もしくは/ブッシュ

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: さあ、今日でこの単元も終わりますね。経済格差について、皆さんはどんな印象を持ちましたか？
lines.en: Well then, we're finishing this unit today. What impressions did everyone get about economic disparity?
lines.style: Polite teacher wrapping up the lesson with an open reflective question to the class.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 正直、経済はまだ素人なんですけど、最近日経新聞を読み始めて、少しずつ流れが見えてきました。
lines.en: Honestly, I'm still an amateur when it comes to economics, but I recently started reading the Nikkei newspaper, and the flow is gradually becoming visible.
lines.style: University student speaking politely and candidly, sharing personal learning progress with natural humility.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 私はブッシュ元大統領の頃の話が一番印象に残ったな。あの時代の政策で得した人達と、損した人達がくっきり分かれてたよね。
lines.en: For me, the stories from around when Bush was president left the strongest impression. The people who benefited and the people who lost out from those policies were clearly divided.
lines.style: Casual teen speech sharing a sharp observation, using sentence-ending na and contracted forms.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: いい着眼点ですね。富を獲得した層と、そこから取り残された層、その背景を理解することが大事ですよ。
lines.en: That's a good point of focus. Understanding the background of the class that acquired wealth and the class left behind from that is what's important.
lines.style: Teacher affirms politely and reframes the student's casual point into more analytical academic language.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: でも先生、全部政策のせいにするのにはちょっと反論したいんです。個人の選択、もしくは運の要素も大きいんじゃないでしょうか。
lines.en: But teacher, I want to push back a little on blaming everything on policy. Aren't individual choices, or factors of luck, also significant?
lines.style: Polite university student respectfully disagreeing, framing his counterargument with hedging and humility.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: えー、でも生まれた家が貧しかったら、それだけで不幸なスタートじゃない？本人のせいじゃないと思うけどな。
lines.en: Huh, but if you're born into a poor family, isn't that already an unfortunate start? I don't think it's the person's own fault.
lines.style: Teenage girl reacting emotionally with sentence-ending na, using casual rhetorical questions.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 二人とも素晴らしい議論ですよ。来週までに、この格差問題について自分の意見をレポートにまとめて提出してくださいね。
lines.en: Both of you are having a wonderful discussion. By next week, please summarize your own opinions on this disparity issue into a report and submit it.
lines.style: Teacher closes the lesson with polite praise and a formal homework assignment using te-kudasai form.
